minutes.headline: Board ratified Thomas Gamel as police chief and recommended Special Town Meeting articles, including the street light purchase.
minutes.summary: The board ratified two appointments, including the permanent police chief, and voted recommendations on Special Town Meeting articles. It reviewed the Bright Farms TIF drafts, adopted a signage policy, and held a workshop on the old primary school site, setting a Halloween site walk. An open meeting law complaint against the Conservation Commission led to a heated exchange before executive session.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 5-0 to recommend several Special Town Meeting articles, including the street light conversion, the capital plan and the sewer reserve deposit.
The board took up the ratification of Thomas Gamel as police chief; the minutes record the vote outcome as not audible.
The board ratified the assessing assistant appointment 5-0 and adopted the signage on town property policy 5-0.
Several articles were left without a recommendation, and the board named an eight-year schedule as its lead option for the Bright Farms TIF.
The board set a members-only site walk of the old primary school site for Oct 31 and an open meeting law complaint led to a heated exchange.

why_it_matters: The recommended articles, especially the street light purchase and how it fixes the stabilization amount, are items residents will be asked to vote on at Special Town Meeting and can affect the tax bill.
The Bright Farms TIF schedule and the old primary school site decisions bear on future tax revenue and on how a town-owned property is used.
watch_next: Nov 3: the board is to choose a date (Dec 1 or Dec 14) for the skateboard park tri-party meeting.
Finance Committee meeting on the 29th, to which the board was invited, and the Special Town Meeting articles still deferred.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the Article 1 recommendation, the signage policy and the main deferrals, but they differ on several votes. The main difference is the Article 19 street light vote, which is 5-0 in ours and 4-1 with Adams opposed in the official minutes. Ours also records 5-0 votes on the assessing assistant, capital plan, Article 10 and salary plan articles that the official minutes do not.
